iCloud sync engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Apple's iCloud workflow covers storefront language. Developer portal, Xcode, and Connect actually separate sync behavior from product-page copy:

  • iCloud capability — toggled in Xcode and linked to your App ID. Controls whether the app can read and write iCloud containers or ubiquitous key-value stores. Does not generate Chinese listing text.
  • CloudKit containers & schema — configured in Apple Developer and CloudKit Dashboard. Separate from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains cross-device sync to buyers.
  • iCloud Drive file provider — document sync and Files app integration in the binary. Your listing may mention it; implementing file-provider extensions is engineering work, not listing copy.
  • Conflict resolution & offline sync — merge logic, CKSyncEngine, and NSUbiquitousKeyValueStore handling in code. AppLocale does not write or debug sync pipelines.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of iCloud capability flags.

A working iCloud sync integration and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.

iCloud sync–specific listing copy — what translates differently

Sync-centric listings use vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers describe Apple's cloud continuity features — not a literal paste of US marketing:

iCloud sync phrasing

US pages use "Sync with iCloud", "Works with iCloud", or "Sync across all your devices." Apple's consumer-facing Simplified Chinese vocabulary uses iCloud 同步 or 与 iCloud 同步 for the feature. AppLocale aligns phrasing with Apple's storefront terms while keeping your app's voice — not inventing sync capabilities your app does not support.

iCloud Drive and document backup

Screenshot overlays and description leads reference file backup — "iCloud Drive", "Files stay in sync", or document-continuity blurbs. Chinese buyers expect concise iCloud 云盘 or 文件自动同步 phrasing rather than English slogans ("Your files, everywhere").

Cross-device continuity claims

Some listings reference iPhone, iPad, and Mac handoff — "Start on iPhone, finish on Mac", "Pick up where you left off", or device-grid screenshots. These are factual product claims in description or screenshot copy — not substitutes for implementing sync in code, which AppLocale does not engineer.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need sync-relevant search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like iCloud 同步, 跨设备, and 云备份 each signal different intent from generic productivity keywords.

Common mistakes on iCloud sync zh-Hans listings

  • Assuming iCloud capability localizes automatically — iCloud enabled in Xcode; zh-Hans row never added or left blank
  • Only translating the description — subtitle, keywords, and screenshot caption lines still English
  • Reusing US sync badges verbatim — Latin "Works with iCloud" badges on zh-Hans screenshots signal an unfinished localization
  • Conflating listing copy with setup instructions — description explains how to enable iCloud in Settings instead of what the buyer gets; setup instructions belong in support docs, not AppLocale scope
  • Overclaiming sync scope — listing promises real-time sync on every platform when the app only syncs notes via NSUbiquitousKeyValueStore; AppLocale rewrites your stated English claims, not invent new ones
  • Ignoring caption fields per localization — zh-Hans screenshot set uploaded but overlay text fields never saved; see Screenshot captions in Simplified Chinese
  • Expecting AppLocale to configure iCloud containers — CloudKit schema, entitlements, and sync conflict code are outside listing rewrite
